research_question: Within two same-encoder prepared development domains, which mechanism best explains weak RARS transport: frozen-candidate headroom, rank capacity, int8 coding, retrieval-objective value, or fit-domain interaction?
scope: outcome-informed mechanism decomposition on opened development evidence; not an independent confirmation, unseen-domain test, universal generalization claim, or production benchmark

parent_evidence.observed_pattern: RARS improves a narrow MS MARCO setting, while setting-specific external diagnostics do not establish a stable advantage over PCA and later global allocation or gating variants fail their gates

evidence_boundary.allowed_claim: which preregistered factor is supported within the two named same-encoder development domains
forbidden_claims: superiority over ScaNN or rebuild-allowed quantizers

factor_matrix.candidate_headroom: same-candidate exact Recall@10 minus Base Recall@10
factor_matrix.rank_capacity: local PCA rank-64 FP32 minus local PCA rank-16 FP32
factor_matrix.int8_coding: local PCA rank-16 FP32 minus the same basis encoded as rank-16 int8
factor_matrix.objective_value: local cutoff-aware RARS rank-16 int8 minus local PCA rank-16 int8
factor_matrix.fit_domain_interaction: local cutoff-aware RARS rank-16 int8 minus source-domain RARS rank-16 int8
factor_matrix.pooled_repair: pooled cutoff-aware RARS rank-16 int8 minus source-domain RARS rank-16 int8

prohibited_actions: changing alpha rank Top-B pair mining or optimization after evaluation outcomes
pooling embeddings from different encoders into one basis
selecting the better domain direction after outcomes
describing this opened-role diagnostic as confirmatory causal evidence
using evaluation outcomes to revise V16
